newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists in failed car bomb escape bid.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists in failed car bomb escape bid.

text.p: A car bomb exploded in central Turkey on Friday in an apparent attempt to free eight Islamist suspects being carried to court in a prison vehicle, Anatolian news agency said.
It said two gendarmerie police were wounded in the attack in the province of Kirsehir. Other gendarmes sealed off the area and prevented the suspects from escaping, the agency said.
"A bomb loaded into a car at the side of the road was set off by remote control...as the armoured prison vehicle was going past," Anatolian said.

The prisoners were being taken to Ankara where they were to appear in a state security court on charges related to the killing of 37 people, most of them members of a liberal, heterodox Moslem sect in an Islamist arson attack in 1993.
Dozens of people have been convicted in the case but the appeals court later called for retrials and tougher sentences.

In Ankara, witnesses said police armoured cars took up position at key spots in the city centre to prevent any Islamist protests after Friday noon prayers at government plans to curb religious education
Police on Tuesday detained more than 50 people at a large Islamist rally in the capital that turned violent.
Islamist anger at Turkey's secularist establishment has risen since Islamist Pime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned under military pressure in June.
He was replaced by secularist Mesut Yilmaz who has vowed to carry out a key military demand to restrict the scope of Islamic schools.
